newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP to wait for Jan data with rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP to wait for Jan data with rate decision.

text.p: The Polish central bank will wait until the release of January statistical data before making a decision on whether it needs to raise nominal interest rates to cool credit growth, its deputy president told the Nowa Europa daily.

"When discussion about interest rates began the rates which we cared about, that is market rates, rose as we intended. But whether this is enough I cannot say," Nowa Europa business daily quoted Witold Kozinski as saying.
"We are waiting for January's statistical data, as this month will give us a snap shot of what is happening with credit in the economy," Kozinski added.

He added that credit action seasonally slows in January, which had to be taken into account when evaluating this month's broad money supply data, due to be released by the central bank in the first half of February.
Broad money supply rose 29 percent last year, while lending to the non-financial sector boomed 44 percent, out of which household credit rose by over 108 percent.

Over the last few weeks the central bank pulled up market rates by some 2.5 percentage points to around 22 percent, but analysts played down the possibililty of an official rate rise after better-than-expected 1996 inflation.
Year-on-year inflation was 18.5 percent last year, down from 21.6 percent at the end of 1995 and against market expectations of around 18.8 percent.
